correctness.rationale: The Euclidean radius-a ball lies in the bicylinder. The exact support reduces to a maximization over a radius-a disk, and a uniform quadratic penalty/Lipschitz argument gives h=a+|s|sqrt(b^2-a^2 sin^2 theta)+O(s^2) with positive minimum linear coefficient. Compactness excludes remote minimizers. Uniform spherical coordinates make the linear tail coefficient and conditional independent marks an immediate change-of-variables limit. Pointwise strict monotonicity of the elliptic integral reconstructs b from the slope. The 121 diagnostic checker assertions are supplementary, not infinite proof; constants may diverge at b=a.

value.rationale: This gives a sharp singular/every-direction boundary for the stereological width distribution of a classical solid with distinct radii. The exact elliptic coefficient, physically interpretable angular localization and independent rare-event mark supply an inverse geometric characterization: only the smallest projection width and its first derivative identify both radii. The diverging slope near equal radii explains the mathematically singular transition to the already established logarithmic law; this is a coherent natural parameter family, not an arbitrary slice.
